- When sentiment turns negative (especially after a spike), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% of recent range.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model often overshoots and forecasts too high — reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 1–3% per day of sustained positivity.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price action — apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags — adjust forecast upward by 1–4% in next 3–5 days.
- Avoid over-relying on recent 30-day mean — sentiment-driven volatility often overrides it — use sentiment-weighted moving average for correction.
